summary: Fallback routing to memory-optimized replica causes cold-start p99 spikes and intermittent 504s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sudden p99 latency regressions and occasional 504s beginning 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC. Symptoms align with traffic spikes and a routing decision that sent requests to a memory-optimized replica group. Impact: degraded user experience for NarrativeAI customers on their dedicated capacity; some requests timed out causing downstream errors in their ingestion pipeline. Hypothesis: fallback routing policy selected a memory-optimized variant that did not have warm replicas available, leading to repeated cold starts and high initialization latency. This was exacerbated by an autoscaler bounce during the traffic surge which drained the warm pool.

Requested action: investigate routing decision logic, verify warm-pool sizes for memory-optimized variant, and provide an interim workaround to the customer while we adjust policies and/or warm pools.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer traffic profile: burst from 600->1800 rps lasting ~10-15 min
2) Force routing policy to allow fallback to 'memory-optimized' variant when latency or capacity thresholds are exceeded
3) Observe that new memory-optimized replicas are scheduled and enter initializing state (GPU warmup + model load) — initial tokens experience large tail latency
4) Some requests hit initialization path and exceed request timeout threshold (30s) leading to 504s
logs: 2026-03-10T08:31:45Z autoscaler: removing idle replicas in warm pool group=memory-optimized-1 reason=scale_down_policy
2026-03-10T08:32:02Z serving-runtime: replica-start pid=27451 model=gptx-7b-sharded stage=loading weights=quantized status=initializing
investigation_notes: Support triage: confirmed customer saw p99 jump from ~450ms to ~12s during the window
Routing logic: policy allowed fallback to memory-optimized variant when primary variant's warm_utilization > 85%
Autoscaler behavior: warm-pool shrink happened ~30s before fallback routing decision; warm replica TTL configured to 60s; observed race between scale-down and fallback decision
KV cache miss rate: increased for memory-optimized variant (no shared prefix cache), so first tokens pay extra cost
Model variant differences: memory-optimized variant uses a larger batch allocator and additional checkpointing during init, increasing cold-start time compared to GPU-optimized variant
comments: Aditi Rao (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported intermittent 504s and p99 spikes starting ~08:30 UTC. Collected request IDs and example payloads. Escalating to SRE for routing/autoscaler investigation.

Evan Kim (SRE) 2026-03-10: Noted autoscaler events removing warm replicas from memory-optimized group. Pulling Grafana traces and scheduler logs. Tentatively: warm pool eviction + fallback selection is the root cause.
Maria Lopez (Customer, NarrativeAI) 2026-03-10: We observed a dozen 504s during our morning campaign. Can you pin us to the previous variant while you investigate? This is production traffic.

Evan Kim (SRE) 2026-03-10: Temporary workaround applied: pinned routing for NarrativeAI to their primary GPU-optimized variant and increased warm_pool_min for memory-optimized group to 2 while we investigate. Asking infra to revert autoscaler aggressive settings for this dedicated capacity.

Aditi Rao (Support) 2026-03-11: Customer confirmed error rate dropped after pinning; monitoring for recurrence. Open action: adjust fallback policy to prefer warm replicas and add pre-warm for memory-optimized variants.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporarily pinned NarrativeAI to the GPU-optimized variant and increased warm_pool_min for memory-optimized replicas to 2. Follow-up: schedule a change to the fallback routing logic so it prefers variants with at least one warm replica and add a cooldown window after scale-downs to prevent race with fallback. Long-term: explore shared prefix cache between variants and a faster init path for memory-optimized replicas.
postmortem_followup_items: Adjust fallback policy to require warm replica before routing
Add warm-pool grace window after scale-down events
Instrument variant selection telemetry to include warm-pool counts
Evaluate prewarming during traffic surges for memory-optimized variants
